effective.effectiveText: Multi-omic integration analyses measurements from different molecular layers, such as DNA, RNA and protein, side by side while keeping track of what each one measured and which specimen it came from.
A variant-effect prediction estimates a defined consequence of a DNA change for a specified transcript or task. It does not by itself establish disease causation or treatment benefit.

Analytical validity concerns whether a test measures reliably. Clinical validity concerns what its result means for a condition or outcome. Clinical utility concerns using that information for a decision.
A virtual cell is a computer model of specified aspects of cells. A predicted response is a model output whose accuracy must be tested against independent measurements.

Training data fit a model, validation data guide choices, and reserved evaluation data test the locked version. The split must match the intended population and prediction task. Choices made using evaluation results make those data part of model development.

External evaluation estimates model performance on data not used to develop or tune it. The patients, setting and methods determine which transportability question it addresses; it does not by itself establish useful clinical decisions.
Cross-validation repeatedly fits a model on part of the data and evaluates it on reserved data. Choices made using those results still belong to model development.

Leakage is when information from the test data reaches the model during training, through a scaler fitted on all samples, a patient split across folds or a benchmark that appeared in the pretraining set, making the model look better than it is.
A drug-response split tests prediction for withheld cell lines, drugs, tissues or pairs. Accuracy on that task does not by itself show clinical benefit or successful drug development.
Drug sensitivity describes response in a specified assay. An IC50 is the concentration producing half-maximal inhibition of its measured endpoint; it does not always mean half the growth.
Calibration checks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies for the same population, outcome and time horizon. Correct ranking or a correct overall average is insufficient.
A computer model can prioritize peptides expected to bind an immune display molecule or appear among its ligands. The prediction helps select candidates for testing.
Multi-omic integration analyses measurements from different molecular layers, such as DNA, RNA and protein, side by side while keeping track of what each one measured and which specimen it came from.
